  "required_fixes": [
    "R1 (high): apps/desktop/src/features/workbench/document-editor.tsx:72-139 loses track of unprotected edit generations. A quick Save cancels the protection timer but leaves marked.current=true, while workbench_domain.rs:1688 clears Rust's editing flag. The next edit sends no Editing request. An older Protect acknowledgement can likewise clear the flag after newer typing. The actual DocumentEditor probe reproduced edit -> Save -> edit with only one Editing request and the second URL still unsaved. The 300 ms native quit guard can therefore allow exit before the 400 ms protection timer. Reconcile protection acknowledgements with the current edit generation and re-arm native dirty tracking after Save. Acceptance: edit-save-edit and typing during an outstanding Protect keep quit guarded until the latest snapshot is durably protected; an older acknowledgement never clears newer unprotected work.",
    "R2 (high): apps/desktop/src/features/workbench/workbench-view.tsx:312,432 closes a collection/tab before DocumentEditor's unmount cleanup protects pending input. workbench_domain.rs:777-784 clears the collection; :854-879 can remove the document when it has no prior draft. The resulting Protect is refused, and closing a collection can lose newer typing even when an older draft exists. Actual WorkbenchView probes recorded openRequest, editing, closeTab/closeCollection, protect, with no successful protection. Protect and acknowledge the fresh snapshot before destructive editor transitions, retaining the editor or offering an explicit discard choice if protection fails. Acceptance: closing either a tab or collection inside the debounce preserves the exact latest text across reopen/restart, including invalid input and private-store failure cases.",
    "R3 (high): crates/desktop-core/src/workbench/project.rs:489 truncates inventory URLs to 2,048 characters; document.rs:356-357 uses inventory method/URL values as authoritative editor fields even though it reads fresh metadata for the baseline. document.rs:513-514 then writes those values back. A header-only Save can truncate a valid 3,000-character URL; a file edited after discovery can similarly have its newer method/URL replaced by stale inventory values. Load authoritative fields from the complete metadata corresponding to the baseline, keeping display abbreviations separate. Acceptance: opening, previewing and saving a URL longer than 2,048 characters preserves it when another field changes; changes made on disk between discovery and opening are loaded faithfully rather than silently reverted.",
    "R4 (high): crates/desktop-core/src/authority/workbench_domain.rs:1588-1674 writes project files before durably protecting the captured Save fields. profile.rs:125-128 journals only paths and hashes; the fresh draft is persisted only after the error return at workbench_domain.rs:1714-1730. If the process stops after the body write but before metadata, a Save performed before the debounce can lose its new URL/headers and cannot reconstruct them from the journal. The current interruption fixture returns Io and then executes the draft-saving handler, so it misses this crash boundary. Durably retain the submitted snapshot before the first project write. Acceptance: restart from the between-write state without running post-error cleanup restores all submitted fields, marks the interruption, writes nothing automatically and permits an explicit recovery choice.",
    "R5 (medium): crates/desktop-core/src/workbench/project.rs:321-332 removes duplicate-ID requests from catalog.requests while leaving complete=true, but document.rs:727-736 uses only catalog.requests to detect shared body ownership. Two valid files with a duplicate ID can consequently disappear from that check; a third request sharing their body can overwrite it. Their diagnostics are also hidden by workbench-view.tsx's !collection.complete condition. Preserve enough ownership evidence to refuse such writes, or mark this inventory unsafe for writes, and expose the duplicate diagnostics. Acceptance: a collection containing only a duplicate pair plus a uniquely identified request sharing their sidecar refuses the body write and leaves all project files unchanged."
  ],
  "blockers": [],
  "evidence_gaps": [
    "E1: docs/architecture/native-checks.json C14-N06 requires both Keep mine and Use disk on conflicts. tools/native-acceptance/acceptance_c14.py:344-364 and native/observations.json demonstrate only Keep mine, while native-acceptance.json marks the combined check passed. Supply native evidence for Use disk on a separate conflict, including the displayed disk version and preserved project/private state, and make the result assertions cover that branch. The Rust deleted-file UseDisk test is useful but does not establish this promised native interaction."
  ],
  "optional_suggestions": [
    "The YAML depth/node-limit mutation survived. Add direct boundary fixtures for MAX_DEPTH and MAX_NODES that pass structural parsing otherwise, so rejection cannot be attributed to another parser or format check. The parent-path mutation is neutralized by the final Component::Normal check and is not evidence of a traversal defect."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Independently recomputed all four fingerprints, verified 502 source-inventory entries and 259 packet references, and checked run input, log and artifact hashes. C13's receipt is a failed 8/10 review accepted under D034 in the completion ledger; its findings remain outstanding for P04. It was not treated as a passing 9/10 review.",
    "Recorded checks include 330 frontend tests, 117 core unit tests, 11 workbench integration tests and 11 focused React tests. These records were inspected, not rerun natively by this reviewer.",
    "Executed independent in-memory probes using the actual DocumentEditor and WorkbenchView with scripted call results; they reproduced the missing post-Save Editing notification and close-before-Protect ordering. Rust persistence, URL truncation and duplicate-sidecar findings were traced in source, not newly executed. No application files were changed, endpoints called or credentials accessed.",
    "Mutation input hashes match the reviewed production files. All 12 baseline executions passed; 29 of 31 mutations were caught. The two survivors are disclosed above rather than counted as killed.",
    "Verified archive checksums and extracted source for serde_yaml_ng 0.10.0, unsafe-libyaml 0.2.11 and ryu 1.0.23. The embedded 193-request SCM catalogue matches v1 revision 74754c02 and SHA-256 914a9ee76723f3fa5bc566806aedbd7c0f7de2f457339c117ac6df3864037a8c.",
    "The native evidence uses staged folder/export selections rather than driving the production rfd sheets; spoken VoiceOver output was not recorded. C14 has no registered performance workload and performs no HTTP execution. C15 execution admission, C25 live qualification and C26 signed-package validation are outside this verdict."
  ],
